Ceiling

Every dollar is tied to an hour

Your only paid offer is a $90 session. Revenue can only grow by adding hours, and there are only so many hours you can give well.

No next step

Free, then a big jump

Your guides and quiz build goodwill, but there’s nothing to buy between a free PDF and booking a session with a counsellor. That’s a big step for someone who has only seen your posts.

Reach

The audience never meets you live

83.9k people follow your work, and none of them get an hour with you in a room before deciding. Reach rises and falls with each post.

People already follow you for how you explain relationships. There’s no low-pressure, paid way yet for them to learn from you directly.

My recommendation

A $17 live masterclass on relationship patterns, a workbook upsell, and an application on the replay page

You don’t have a paid low-ticket product yet, so the seat itself should be paid. It’s education, not therapy: 90 minutes on why relationship patterns repeat, in the voice people already follow. The seats and the workbook pay for the ads, and the replay page invites the right people to apply for a free 15-minute consultation.

Who it’s for

For anyone curious about how relationships work

  • You want to understand why some relationship dynamics feel so familiar.
  • You’re curious about attachment theory and want it explained in plain language.
  • You’d like simple language for talking about needs and boundaries.
  • You want to understand a partner, friend or family member a little better.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover together

Where relationship patterns come from

How early experiences shape what we expect from the people closest to us, explained without jargon.

Attachment styles, explained

The four styles researchers describe, what they look like in everyday life, and why they’re a lens, not a label.

Why familiar can feel like chemistry

Why we’re often drawn to what we already know, and how to tell the difference between comfort and fit.

Needs, boundaries and the awkward first time

Why setting a boundary can feel uncomfortable at first, and simple words for asking for what you need.

A reflection practice you can keep

A short, simple practice for noticing patterns as they happen, so you can pause and choose.

Meet your host

Hi, I’m Diksha

I’m a registered counsellor (ACA Level 2) based in Melbourne. I hold a Bachelor of Arts with Psychology (Honours) and a Master of Counselling, and I’ve trained in the Gottman Method for couples (Level 1 and Level 2), plus DBT, ACT and CBT.

On Instagram I share what I’ve learned about relationships, self-worth and emotions with a community of 83.9k. This masterclass is the longer version: one live session where I can explain it properly and answer your questions.

“A lot of what we call chemistry is really familiarity. We’re drawn to what we already know, and that’s one reason relationship patterns repeat. Once you understand where they come from, they get a lot easier to notice.”
